o1.biggest_strength: It handles the trade-offs honestly and puts the break-in note above the fold. The 'What to know before you buy' block and the 'snug, ease in over about a week' bullet go straight at the two biggest return causes.
o1.biggest_mistake: Customer-facing copy says the hidden pocket takes 'one more flat note', which is an invented capacity on the exact cash question we are trying to stop overstating. The SEO title also runs slightly past 60 characters.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Drop the extra-note claim, use Tom's 'brick in my back pocket' phrase, and put the first-week break-in note in the line under the button.

o2.biggest_strength: It treats about 10 flat notes as the total, hidden pocket included, so the page never overstates cash. It also uses the customer's own 'brick in your back pocket' line, gives inch conversions for US buyers, and checks the SEO lengths.
o2.biggest_mistake: The break-in expectation sits in the description, what-fits section and FAQ but not in a bullet or the under-button line, so a fast buyer can still miss it. The 10 to 11 mm figure for 6 or 7 cards is interpolated rather than given in the data.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Add 'Slots start snug and settle in about a week' to the card bullet or under the button, and measure lift against a holdout rather than a before-and-after comparison.

reason: Both are strong and honest about cash, but the second never inflates capacity, uses my customers' own words, and tells me how to check whether returns actually drop. The first's extra-note claim is the kind of overstatement that brings returns back.
